=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Baseline:** Acquisition of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd for AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law.

## Preliminary points

- **The "FINAL" label and market-norm claims don't bind us.** The preamble says the positions were "settled at principal level" and "not intended to be re-opened," but nothing is agreed until the SPA is signed. The market-range assertions (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 month limitation periods) are the Seller's characterisation and should be tested by our deal team, not accepted.
- **The diligence record is stale.** Facts are stated as at 22 September 2026 and today is 5 November 2026. Every disclosed item needs a bring-down and current confirmation before we rely on it.
- **Several items are already unresolved and may be time-critical.** The Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment and privacy assessment are all open.

## Material departures from Buyer interests

| # | Issue | Seller position | Why it departs from our interests | Our position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **General cap (12.1)** | AUD 4.8M (20%) | At the top of the Seller's own range, and the known issues below could consume most of it. | Push for a higher cap (at least 30%) or cap at purchase price for general warranties; fundamental, tax and specific matters outside this cap. |
| 2 | **De minimis and basket (12.2)** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible-style basket | Only the excess is recoverable, so the first AUD 250k of losses is absorbed by us. | Tipping basket (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar) at around 0.5–1% of price; lower de minimis; small claims count toward the basket. |
| 3 | **Time limits (12.3/13)** | 18 months for all claims, applied across the board | Too short for tax (ATO amendment periods run longer) and for privacy and regulatory exposure, which may surface late. | General warranties 24–36 months; tax to ATO period plus a margin; fundamental and title to the NSW contract limitation period (verify under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW)). |
| 4 | **Fundamental/title warranties** | Same cap and time limits as general warranties | Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying. Subjecting them to a 20% cap is unacceptable. | Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price, with full limitation period. |
| 5 | **Exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5)** | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Would cover fraud and potentially statutory claims. | Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, specific indemnities and tax. Confirm non-reliance cannot exclude misleading or deceptive conduct claims under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18 applies to conduct in trade or commerce; verify application to this transaction). |
| 6 | **Data room disclosure (Schedule 7, DL 1.1–1.2)** | Discloses everything in the data room and public registers | Makes the buyer's warranty protection hollow. We would be treated as accepting every data-room fact. | Reject general disclosure. Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly and specifically described, with the data room made available only as a reference point. |
| 7 | **Buyer knowledge (8.3)** | No claim for matters known or discoverable by the Buyer or its advisers | Anti-sandbagging. Combined with item 6, it would bar claims on exactly the issues we have now identified. | Express pro-sandbagging clause: buyer's rights are unaffected by knowledge or diligence. Reject "discoverable" as a standard. |
| 8 | **Bluefen (cl. 3/6.3; DL 2)** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; treats consent as satisfied on delivery of written consent | 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6M) depends on change-control consent; the conditions in clause 11.3 are not addressed at all. | Written consent and satisfaction of 11.3 conditions as a condition precedent, with a termination right if not met by a long-stop date. If waived, price adjustment or escrow. |
| 9 | **Riverlark (cl. 2/7; DL 3)** | ~AUD 3.2M facility; release to be provided *after* Completion | Debt-free/cash-free requires payoff at Completion. Post-Completion release leaves us exposed on the security and effectively funds the debt on top of the price. | Payoff letter and discharge of security (including PPSR removal) delivered at Completion, with payout deducted from the price in the funds flow. |
| 10 | **Ironquay IP (11.1; DL 4)** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open); "considered adequate" | Project Materials transfer is conditional on payment, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists. The indemnity doesn't address IP ownership or infringement. | Pay the AUD 180k at or before Completion as a debt-like item. Confirmatory assignment as a condition precedent. Specific IP-title indemnity outside the cap and basket. |
| 11 | **Employee bonuses (DL 5)** | AUD 420k, "a matter for the Seller," not in funds flow | Completion bonuses are debt-like. Payroll tax and superannuation on-costs are unaddressed. Indicatively, superannuation guarantee at 12% adds about AUD 50k on top of the bonuses, plus any payroll tax (verify NSW rates with tax advisers). | Include bonuses and on-costs as debt-like items in net debt. Seller bears these. |
| 12 | **Privacy incident (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6; DL 6)** | "Preliminary, not expected to be material"; ~1,240 records possibly exposed; no assessment completed | Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme, an assessment must be completed within 30 days of suspicion. If the incident was known around 22 September, that window may already have passed, and the liability sits in the company we are buying. The data (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) may still trigger notification. | Pre-Completion forensic investigation and NDB assessment. Specific indemnity for regulatory, notification and third-party loss, outside cap and basket. Warranty that no notifiable data breach has occurred, or full disclosure of one. Seek urgent privacy counsel advice. |
| 13 | **Office lease (DL 7)** | Notification obligation only | Landlord consent may be needed if the change of control triggers a clause. | Confirm with the lease. Landlord consent (or waiver) as a condition precedent if required. |
| 14 | **Supplier renewals (DL 8)** | AUD 330k (3 × 110k) treated as ordinary course | Renewals may be committed costs, and the Seller is not stating whether they are terminable or accrued. | Review each contract. Costs attributable to pre-Completion periods, or non-terminable commitments, to be borne by the Seller or treated as debt-like. |
| 15 | **Mossvale (DL 9)** | Assignment restriction; consent not stated as required | A share sale may still trigger change-of-control terms. | Confirm the clause. Consent as a condition precedent if triggered. |
| 16 | **Title (DL 10)** | Share register at DD-012 relied on | The register shows the Seller's holding, but we have not verified it. | Independent verification (ASIC searches, register inspection, confirmation of no encumbrances). Title warranty as fundamental. |
| 17 | **Tax and IP** | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax and IP exposures are not covered by the general regime as drafted. | Stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, outside cap and basket, with limitation aligned to the ATO amendment period. Separate IP warranties. |
| 18 | **Funds flow** | "Reflects the agreed price mechanics" | It does not reflect the Riverlark payout, the bonuses, the Ironquay payment or the supplier costs. | Rebuild funds flow with a full net debt schedule. |

## Exposure check

Quantifiable known items:

- Riverlark: AUD 3.2M
- Employee bonuses: AUD 0.42M (plus on-costs)
- Ironquay: AUD 0.18M
- Supplier renewals: AUD 0.33M (if treated as pre-Completion)

Total: about **AUD 4.1M**, close to the AUD 4.8M general cap.

Because the disclosure letter discloses these matters, warranty claims would likely fail for them. They must be dealt with through price adjustment, debt-like items or specific indemnities, not general warranty recovery. Bluefen revenue exposure and privacy exposure are not yet quantified.

## Recommendations (summary)

1. **Reject the "FINAL" framing.** Treat all Seller positions as open for negotiation.
2. **Reject general data-room disclosure and anti-sandbagging.** Insist on specific disclosure and an express pro-sandbagging clause.
3. **Raise the general cap and move to a tipping basket.** Carve fundamental warranties, tax, fraud and specific indemnities out of the cap and time limits.
4. **Make Bluefen consent and Mossvale/landlord consents conditions precedent**, with a termination right.
5. **Pay out Riverlark at Completion** through the funds flow, with discharge of security at Completion.
6. **Treat the bonuses, Ironquay AUD 180k and relevant supplier costs as debt-like items.** Rebuild the funds flow.
7. **Obtain specific indemnities** for the privacy incident, Ironquay IP, tax, and the title/capacity warranties.
8. **Commission urgent privacy assessment** and forensic review before Completion.
9. **Bring down all diligence** to current date and verify title independently.
10. **Have NSW counsel verify** the statutory points above (limitation periods, Australian Consumer Law, Privacy Act timing, payroll tax and superannuation rates) before the mark-up goes out.
